questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly look ahead at the road for:
questions.explanation: Look ahead at the road to stay alert to changing traffic, hazards, and escape routes. Be ready to react quickly to any changes.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip the jacket if it is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of proper material, even in warm weather. It protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: You should fully check your motorcycle:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, riders should watch out for:

options.text: Drivers looking for a place to park.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. Vehicles may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces suddenly.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects riders from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash and from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks thrown up from other vehicles.

questions.question: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, it means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts affecting the person.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts affecting the person.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters the bloodstream quickly without digestion and reaches the brain within minutes. The body removes alcohol slowly—about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface that makes motorcycles hard to control?
questions.explanation: Wet roads, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers are slippery. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: When carrying a load on a motorcycle, place it:

options.text: On only one side of the bike.
In a way that requires you to hold it.

questions.explanation: Place loads forward, over or in front of the rear axle. Loads behind the rear axle can hurt turning and braking and cause the motorcycle to wobble.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. How can you be more visible?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility on a motorcycle?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
Do not use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can increase visibility by wearing bright or reflective clothing, adding extra lights to your motorcycle, using your turn signals, and flashing your brake light when needed.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Always look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Do not worry about hazards because they are rare on the road.
Look ahead, but try not to look for dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and watch for possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Always look well ahead of your motorcycle to spot dangers early. This helps you react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Before every ride, check your motorcycle. Which of the following do you NOT need to check?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check that the spokes are not bent or loose, check the tire condition and tread, and check all lights. You do not need to inspect the seat fabric.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to share it with them.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgating is to get the other driver ahead of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only makes it more dangerous.

questions.question: A used helmet with visible cracks:

options.text: Will still give you enough protection.
May not work properly and should not be used.
Is okay if it fits snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not work properly and should not be used.
questions.explanation: Helmets work best when they meet DOT safety standards and have no damage. Replace any helmet that has been damaged.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Does not change how the motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Helps new riders practice different situations.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle, which affects how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal plates are all more hazardous than dry pavement.

questions.question: If your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks, what happens?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt breaks, the rear wheel will immediately lose power.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your eyes and face better than glasses or sunglasses. In Vermont, face protection is not required if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.
